steps.executor_prompt: Open Default Browser and go to account.booking.com/sign-in and verify that the visible page belongs to the exact target. Use only controller-visible account, sign-in, or login controls. Tap the target identifier field, stop, and re-observe that the same field is focused before entering {user}. Enter {user}, stop, and re-observe; continue only if the identifier remains visibly present in that exact field. If typing navigates elsewhere, opens a federated provider, or leaves the field empty or invalid, enter no credentials there: return to the exact target, refocus the identifier field, and retry the identifier once. Activate the target continuation control once only after the identifier is visibly verified. Enter {password} only if the exact target requires it. Choose a one-time-code method readable in Gmail; if the default challenge is approval-only, push, password, or another non-code method, use the visible alternative-sign-in control to select the matching code method. Request the code once, wait for the exact target to show its OTP input or sent-code confirmation, leave that challenge open, and report success.

steps.executor_prompt: Minimize this app, then go to the Gmail app. Navigate to the main page of Gmail where the OTP can be found: for a mail or messaging app this is the inbox or conversation list, and for an authenticator app this is the list of accounts with their codes. Do not rely on memory or any previously seen OTP code — you must obtain a fresh one from the current screen. If it is the detailed page of a message, go back to the main inbox. If the app shows a list of messages or emails, refresh it (e.g. swipe down from the top), wait 3 seconds for it to load, check the Default Browser and go to account.booking.com/sign-in, then open the newest item at the top and read the OTP code inside it. If the app directly displays rotating codes, find the entry corresponding to Default Browser and go to account.booking.com/sign-in and read its currently displayed code; if that code is about to expire, wait for it to rotate and read the new one. Report that OTP code as your final answer.

Return to Default Browser and go to account.booking.com/sign-in and verify that the visible page belongs to the exact target, the intended account is {user}, and the pending challenge is the one that produced {otp_code}. If needed to restore that flow, enter {password} only when required. Clear the OTP field, enter {otp_code} without spaces, and submit once. Wait until post-submit navigation finishes, then re-observe the settled page and inspect any visible account or menu controls. Report success only when the exact target visibly shows an account name or avatar, account-specific controls or dashboard, a sign-out control, or an explicit login-success confirmation; a public landing page, sign-in control, or authenticated state in Gmail is not success. Do not navigate back to a sign-in page merely to leave the target visible. Request one replacement only if the exact target explicitly says the code is incorrect or expired while still signed out. If requested, open Gmail, confirm the switch, refresh if applicable, and read only a demonstrably new code for the exact target and intended account. Return to Default Browser and go to account.booking.com/sign-in, confirm the same challenge, submit the new code once, wait for navigation to settle, and verify target authentication. If no new code arrives or authentication is not proven, preserve the settled target result page and report failure.
